sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:10

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:10:1
items.html:
And then it is necessary that the Nukva of Keter too receive from her upper root: This means that this whole great coupling, which was made upon the screen shared of male and female together, and which drew the great light of the upper Keter, as has been explained — behold, it all remained in the Rosh [head] and cannot expand to the Guf [body], for the reason that the aspect of the coarseness of drawing of phase four is lacking there. And the matter of the sharing that was made with the aspect of drawing of phase three sufficed for the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, since there is in them no aspect of clothing in actuality; but it does not suffice for clothing in actuality within the Guf.
And therefore, at the very time when there awoke in the male of the vessel of Keter the aspect of the coarseness of clothing, to expand with this great light to the aspect of clothing in actuality — the meaning of which is to clothe in the ten Sefirot of the Guf — there became recognisable immediately, because of this, also the aspect of the Guf included in the light of Keter, which stands in the place of the Malchut of the Rosh, as above; whereby its form changed from the Malchut of the Rosh, and it is discerned by this that it parted immediately from Malchut and went out from there to its own place, for disparity of form separates and divides spiritual things one from another. And since it went out from the place of Malchut, it is found that it was immediately separated from the light of the upper Keter, and there remained in it only the previous restricted illumination — which is called that the light of Keter turned its face upward and its posterior downward, as written before us.
And this is what he says, “and then it is necessary that the Nukva of Keter too receive from the upper root.” That is, as written, that the coupling is not completed by the great coupling of the level of the upper Keter, since its illumination does not expand to the Guf; and therefore the coupling made upon the aspect of the female of Keter is needed — that is, upon the coarseness of phase three, which is complete both in the aspect of drawing and in the aspect of clothing.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:10:2
items.html: From her upper root, which is Hochma. As written above, that the record which remained from the level of Hochma of the first expansion after its departure, which is the aspect of the coarseness of phase three, is the one that here becomes the aspect of the Nukva of Keter, and she is the source of this second expansion.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:10:3
items.html:
The root of the upper Hochma descends into Bina, and Bina into Hesed, etc. That is to say, that the aspect of the coupling made upon the aspect of the female of Keter, who is phase three, causes the descent of the degrees from beginning to end: that Keter descends to the degree of Hochma, and Hochma descends to the degree of Bina, and Bina descends to the degree of Hesed, and so forth, until Yesod descends to the degree of Malchut.
And the reason for the matter is that this coupling, which is made upon the coarseness of phase three, does not raise reflected light and does not draw anything but the level of Hochma. And therefore it is found, from the aspect of this coupling, that the light of Hochma descends and clothes in the vessel of Keter, and it is discerned that Keter descended from its degree and came to the degree of Hochma; and likewise the light of Bina clothes in the vessel of Hochma, and the Sefira of Hochma descended to the degree of Bina; and so forth, until the light of Malchut clothed in the vessel of Yesod, and Yesod descended to the degree of Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:10:4
items.html:
Keter, etc., for it has no likeness with the root of Malchut. For at the time of the ascent of the screen and the Sefirot upward to the Emanator — the meaning of which is that they were refined entirely of every aspect of the coarseness of the Guf [body], that is, from above downward, whereby they came into equivalence of form with the Malchut of the Rosh [head] — it is therefore discerned that the light of the level of Keter that rose from the Guf came into the place of Malchut, it being then refined like Malchut, and there is no disparity of form at all between them, as the ARI says above in item 9, where he wrote, “and this is drawn to it by that Keter which remained above at the end of the roots being refined” (and see there in the Inner Light, page 299, in the passage beginning “And this is what he says here”). However, after the first coupling mentioned was completed, which drew the level of the upper Keter in the aspect of from below upward that applies in the Rosh, then its time came to turn about and expand also from above downward, the meaning of which is to clothe in the Guf, as applies in all couplings, as is known. And behold, then the light of Keter that is in the place of the Malchut of the Rosh awoke to return and expand to the Guf as it had been there at first. However, since the aspect of the Nukva of the Rosh was not in her place in phase four — for the phase four of the aspect of drawing was lacking there (as above in the Inner Light, page 300, the passage beginning “And then it is necessary”) — she was therefore unable to expand from above downward into ten Sefirot from herself and within herself down to the Tabur of the Guf, and all the great light of this coupling remained in the Rosh.
However, since the light of Keter mentioned awoke to return and expand to the Guf as at first, then even though it did not return, this awakening nevertheless caused it to reveal the coarseness of the Guf that was in it from the time it had been there at first; and since the coarseness of the Guf was revealed in it, behold, its form changed by this from the Malchut of the Rosh, and it has no further likeness with her, for it became as distant from her as the aspect of the Guf is distant from the aspect of the Rosh.
And this is what he says, “and then that Keter which rose to the place of the root of Malchut descends to its place, for it cannot be there, since it has no likeness with the root of Malchut, and moreover it is a branch and Malchut is a root.” Which is as above, that after the coupling was completed the coarseness of the Guf awoke in it, and its form changed from Malchut until it has no further likeness with her, and therefore it must of necessity descend from there and return to its place. And this is what he says, “for this is a root and this is a branch,” for the aspect of the Guf is a branch and the aspect of the Rosh is a root.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:10:5
items.html: It descends to its place. Which is beneath the vessel of the Malchut of the Rosh [head], that is, an aspect intermediate between Rosh and Guf [body]. For to the Guf it cannot descend and expand, for the reason that the Nukva of the Rosh does not expand into ten Sefirot of her reflected light so as to be vessels to clothe it, as above in the adjacent passage; and in the Rosh it cannot be, for the reason of the disparity of form mentioned. And therefore it is discerned as an intermediate aspect between them.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:10:6
items.html: That all of them are equal in their reception from the root of the upper Keter. This means that before the second coupling was made upon the screen of the coarseness of phase three — that is, upon the aspect of the female of Keter alone — behold, the female is still included with the phase four of the male, and the male of Keter is included in the light of Keter, as above; and therefore all three of them are now equal in their reception from the upper Keter, that is to say, in the aspect of what they still receive from the level of Keter of the Rosh [head].
